title: Equal shares: halves, thirds, and fourths

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A whole is all of one thing. This rectangle is one whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cut it into two equal shares, called halves.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now slide one share over the other. It covers it exactly.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Equal means the same size, the same amount.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each share is one half. Two halves make the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three equal shares are thirds. One, two, three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each share is one third. Three thirds make the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four equal shares are fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three, four. Four fourths make the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The name counts the equal shares in the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These three parts are unequal: different sizes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide the small part onto the big one. Some stays uncovered.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three parts, but not thirds. Thirds must be equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Shaded means colored in. One share is one third.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two shaded shares: two thirds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Thirds means three equal shares, colored or uncolored.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three shaded: three thirds, the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These squares are the same size. Each has one half shaded.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rectangle half here; a triangle half there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cut the triangle here. Turn this piece to fill the gap.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide them over. They cover the rectangle half exactly.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Changing the shape did not change how much was there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which shape is cut into thirds?

do.text: Which shape is cut into thirds?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I choose shape A. I see three pieces there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three pieces are not enough. In A, one piece is bigger than the others.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Shape B is cut into four equal parts. Those are fourths.

do.text: Which shape is cut into thirds?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: C has three equal shares. I choose C here.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two equal shares: halves. Three: thirds. Four: fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Equal shares are the same size. The name counts how many make the whole.

do.text: Count equal shares in the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count equal shares, then name the amount.
